# tests/qemu-boot.expected -- required substrings for a healthy QEMU boot log.
# One literal substring per line; blank lines and '#' comments are ignored.
# Checked by tools/check-boot-log.sh via `grep -aF` (the log interleaves raw
# single-char tick bytes, so it must be forced to text). Substrings stop just
# before the first run-variable field (ttbr0_pa / child_e / entry / freed / at);
# nr= values are fixed boot-table slots (kernel-shared/src/com.rs).

# Kernel banner (kernel/src/main.rs)
minix.rs booting on aarch64

# Address-space bring-up: 9 servers + init (arch/aarch64/userland.rs). The tty
# line is new in slice 5.3 and the memory line in 5.7 -- the two user-space
# *drivers*, packed between ds and vfs so each is in its receive loop before its
# first client (which is vfs for both).
[as] vm nr=7 ttbr0_pa=
[as] ds nr=5 ttbr0_pa=
[as] tty nr=4 ttbr0_pa=
[as] memory nr=3 ttbr0_pa=
[as] vfs nr=1 ttbr0_pa=
[as] sched nr=9 ttbr0_pa=
[as] rs nr=2 ttbr0_pa=
[as] pm nr=0 ttbr0_pa=
[as] init nr=10 ttbr0_pa=

# ...plus the 4 boot stubs (13 [as] lines total)
[as] stub A nr=11 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub B nr=12 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub C nr=13 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub D nr=14 ttbr0_pa=

# init's fork/exec/wait cycle (head-carved kernel traces; slot 15 is the
# fork-pool base, recycled every cycle; exec renames the child to "worker")
[ksys SYS_FORK] parent=i nr=10 child_nr=15
[ksys SYS_EXEC] target=15 name=worker entry=
[ksys SYS_EXIT] target=w nr=15 freed=

# Stub D's designed SIGSEGV chain: page fault -> VM -> SYS_KILL sig=11 -> PM
# tears the stub down with SYS_EXIT
[pf] proc=D far=
[ksys SYS_KILL] target=D nr=14 sig=11 -> pm
[ksys SYS_EXIT] target=D nr=14 freed=

# RS's periodic kernel alarm: assert only the FIRST fire (always inside the
# head carve-out) -- timing-robust under slow CI TCG, unlike a fire count
[alarm 1] owner=r nr=2 at=

# Slice 5.1: stub A's one-shot bad-pointer probes. Each returns EFAULT instead
# of taking an EL1 data abort (which the forbidden list catches as a panic).
# Between them they cover every arm of the copy engine: probe 1 is a fully
# unmapped page, probe 2 straddles A's stack page into the unmapped one above
# it, probe 3 fails in the deferred MF_DELIVERMSG flush and lands EFAULT in A's
# parked x0, and probe 4 names A's *mapped but read-only* code page -- the only
# check on that path is the copy engine's own Prot::writable test, since the
# kernel writes through the HHDM alias where EL0 permission bits do not apply.
# call=1 is SEND; nr=11 is stub A. These lines are unsampled, so unlike
# `[ipc N]` they cannot drift with IPC ordering.
[efault] proc=A nr=11 call=1 va=0x900000
[efault] proc=A nr=11 call=1 va=0x800ff8
[efault deliver] proc=A nr=11 va=0x900000
[efault deliver] proc=A nr=11 va=0x400000

# Slice 5.1: SYS_DIAGCTL is real -- every SEF server announces itself from EL0
# through the kernel debug channel. The name prefix comes from the kernel's own
# proc slot, not the payload, so these lines cannot be spoofed. Assert two of
# the six: vm is the first server packed in the MXBI archive, pm the last, so
# together they bracket the whole roster.
[diag vm] sef ready
[diag pm] sef ready

# Slice 5.2: the grant engine, end to end. VFS direct-grants PM a 64-byte
# read-only buffer and hands the id over in a PM_GRANT_TEST message; PM reads it
# through the grant, then reads the *same* bytes again with the ungranted
# SYS_COPY and compares. `match=1` is the whole point — it proves the grant path
# moved the right bytes, not merely some bytes. Registration is per-granter, so
# both VFS (proc=1) and PM (proc=0) appear; assert VFS's, which is the one the
# demo's grant is served from.
[ksys SYS_SETGRANT] proc=1 entries=
[ksys SYS_SAFECOPY] granter=
[ksys SYS_COPY] src=
[diag pm] grant.test ok
[diag pm] copy ok match=1

# ...and the magic (third-party) arm: PM grants *itself* access to init's text
# page and safecopies out of init's address space, a process that granted
# nothing. Only the length is asserted — the bytes are init's instruction
# encodings and change whenever init is rebuilt. Without this line the magic
# path would be dead code until slice 5.5.
[diag pm] magic ok

# Slice 5.2: the copies that must be REFUSED. Seven safecopies, each valid in
# every respect but one. Five are EPERM from `verify_grant` — wrong grantee,
# wrong access, stale sequence, out-of-range index, past the end of the granted
# range — and two are EFAULT from the copy engine itself: a granter claiming
# CPF_WRITE over its own read-only .rodata (only `Prot::writable` stands between
# that lie and a corrupted page, since the kernel copies through the HHDM alias)
# and a well-formed grant over an unmapped page. Remove any one of those checks
# and that copy succeeds, so this line turns into `grant.deny FAIL <which>` and
# the marker disappears. (The `CPF_INDIRECT` and magic-`SYS_PROC` arms are not
# probed; see `grant_denials` in servers/pm for why neither is reachable yet.)
[diag pm] grant.deny ok

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slice 5.3: the TTY console driver and the CDEV band.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The driver announces itself on the kernel debug channel, exactly like the six SEF
# servers. Distinct from the console banner below: this one proves TTY reached
# `sef_startup`, before it has touched any hardware.
[diag tty] sef ready

# The kernel pre-maps the PL011's MMIO page into TTY's address space with Device
# attributes (there is no VMCTL_MAP_PHYS -- D1 deferred VM-mediated device mapping
# to Phase 6, so this is a bring-up step like the stack page). va/pa are fixed
# constants (uspace::TTY_UART_VA, uart::PL011_PHYS_BASE) so both are asserted; the
# attr_idx is NOT, because which MAIR index already encodes a Device type depends on
# what the bootloader programmed. Delete this pre-map, or weaken it to a
# non-writable Prot, and TTY's first register store takes an EL0 data abort -- which
# the forbidden list catches.
[devmap] tty va=0x40000000 pa=0x9000000 attr_idx=

# TTY never exits, so `teardown_addrspace`'s device arm would be untested code on a
# live landmine: a missing `prot.device` guard makes `free_frame` panic on the
# UART's PA. `userland::device_teardown_selftest` therefore builds one throwaway
# address space holding exactly one device leaf and tears it down at boot. Both
# counts are asserted -- freed=0 proves the leaf was NOT freed, devs=1 proves it was
# actually seen (a guard that skipped every leaf would give freed=0 devs=0).
# Unconditional, so the --no-default-features boot covers it too.
[devmap] selftest ok freed=0 devs=1

# The milestone. Every other line in this log carries a kernel trace prefix
# ([as] / [ipc] / [ksys] / [diag] / [pf] / [devmap]); this one was composed at EL0
# and reached the wire through a user-space store to a device register.
minix.rs console: tty online (EL0)

# Slice 5.3: VFS drives the console over CDEV_WRITE. It resolves TTY through DS
# rather than hard-coding boot_endpoint(TTY_PROC_NR) -- what a real client does. The
# lookup is not deterministic by construction (it works because build.rs packs tty
# before vfs), so a failed lookup falls back to the boot endpoint and emits
# `cdev.ds FAIL` instead: the demo still runs, and *this* marker disappears, so an
# ordering regression turns CI red specifically rather than silently passing.
[diag vfs] cdev.ds ok ep=

# A real write: a read-only direct grant over VFS's banner, and a reply compared
# against the granted length. `match=1` rather than the length itself -- self-
# checking, and independent of the banner text. A driver replying OK instead of the
# byte count gives match=0.
[diag vfs] cdev.write ok match=1

# The short-write contract: VFS asks for CDEV_MAX_IO + 8 bytes and must get exactly
# CDEV_MAX_IO back. That is what lets a driver stage through a fixed buffer with no
# allocator, and it is the difference between "write returns a count" and "write
# returns success". Change the clamp and this number changes with it.
[diag vfs] cdev.short ok n=256

# ...and the two requests that must be REFUSED, each valid in every respect but
# one: minor 7 with a perfectly good grant (ENXIO, from TTY's own minor check), and
# a grant issued to PM rather than TTY (EPERM, from the kernel's `who_to` check --
# the property that makes a grant id safe to pass around at all). Remove either
# check and that request succeeds, so this line becomes `cdev.deny FAIL <name>`.
[diag vfs] cdev.deny ok n=2

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slice 5.4: the POSIX write path -- init -> VFS -> TTY, with one copy.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# These three lines are written BY init, THROUGH the path they test. init holds no
# kernel calls and no grant table (the shared USER priv), so it has no debug
# channel: `write()` is its only way to speak, and a regression takes the evidence
# with it rather than reporting on itself.
#
# Asserted substrings are kept short on purpose. The log interleaves raw kernel
# tick bytes, and TTY's EL0 stores can be preempted mid-line, so a whole-line match
# is not reliable -- the same rule the [as]/[ksys] markers follow.

# The milestone: a user process put bytes on the console under its own POSIX call.
# VFS resolved fd 1, issued a MAGIC grant naming init's buffer with TTY as grantee,
# and TTY safecopied straight out of init's address space -- VFS never touched the
# bytes. The grant's owner comes from the kernel-stamped m_source; read it from a
# payload field instead and every line in this block vanishes (EPERM: the grant
# would name the wrong owner).
minix.rs init: hello via VFS write

# A line longer than one CDEV_WRITE can carry. CDEV_MAX_IO is a driver staging
# detail and must not leak into write()'s return, so VFS re-sends with `offset`
# advanced until the buffer is out. This tail marker sits past the clamp: drop
# VFS's loop and the console gets the first 256 bytes while this substring -- and
# only this substring -- disappears.
vfs-loop-end

# ...and the count that write returned, checked by init against what it asked for.
# The other half of the same contract, and neither half subsumes the other: a
# write() that moved every byte but replied OK would still print the tail above
# while lying to a caller looping on the result. `match=1` rather than the number
# itself is the 5.3 convention -- self-checking, and init has no way to format an
# integer anyway (no server-rt, so no diag_fmt).
minix.rs init: vfs.long ok match=1

# Four refusals, then the summary on fd 2 (so that descriptor is proven too).
# Each probe is well-formed but for one field: descriptor 3 (in range of the fd
# row, not open -> EBADF), a request number one past VFS_WRITE (-> ENOSYS, and the
# reply itself is the assertion -- a dropped unknown request would block init
# forever and hang the boot), an unmapped buffer (-> EFAULT from the kernel's
# page-table walk, relayed back through TTY and VFS unflattened; it costs init no
# page fault, since the copy engine walks rather than dereferences), and a negative
# length (-> EINVAL, which unchecked would widen into a ~16 EiB u64 on the grant).
# A missing check makes its probe succeed and turns this into
# `vfs.deny FAIL <name>`. A zero-length write is deliberately not probed here --
# it is a legal no-op, not a denial, and `write::validate` covers it (and the
# check order that keeps it from issuing a grant) in host tests.
minix.rs init: vfs.deny ok n=4

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slice 5.5: the exec ABI -- a SysV initial stack, so musl's crt runs unpatched.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The kernel's half: SYS_EXEC now builds [argc][argv][NULL][envp NULL][auxv]
# [AT_NULL] on the new image's stack page and points sp_el0 at it. auxv=4 is the
# full set -- AT_PHDR/AT_PHNUM/AT_PHENT/AT_PAGESZ -- and the first three appear
# only because userland/worker/user.ld uses the `FILEHDR PHDRS` idiom, so the
# first PT_LOAD covers the ELF header. Revert that link change and this becomes
# auxv=1: the count is what makes the conditional arm observable rather than
# quietly dead. sp is last because it is the run-variable field.
[exec] argc=1 envc=0 auxv=4 sp=0x

# ...and the EL0 half, which is the one that actually proves anything: the trace
# above only says the kernel *thinks* it wrote a frame. `worker`'s _start is
# naked (`mov x0, sp` is the first instruction it runs, so no prologue can
# perturb the value) and it checks the frame byte for byte -- alignment, argc,
# the argv[0] string, both NULL terminators, AT_PAGESZ, and a phdr readable at
# AT_PHDR. The verdict leaves as its exit status rather than a console line,
# because worker runs once per init fork cycle; init reaps that child -- matched
# by pid, since PM parents the demo stubs to init and stub D's early SIGSEGV
# would otherwise be the first thing reaped -- and prints its status once. A
# failing check turns this into `exec stack FAIL code=N` (forbidden), naming
# which property broke. Success is the positive sentinel EXEC_STACK_PROBE_PASS,
# not 0: PM's kill path zombifies a signalled process without setting
# exit_status, so a worker that faulted before reporting is reaped with 0 --
# which prints `exec stack FAIL no-verdict` rather than passing silently.
minix.rs init: exec stack ok

# --- slice 5.6: the first C program on minix.rs (milestone A) -------------

# `init` alternates its exec target between `worker` and `hello` (EXEC_TARGETS),
# so 5.5's exec-stack probe above stays live alongside the C milestone. Both
# land inside do_exec's 6-call head carve-out, so both traces appear.
#
# Deliberately NOT keyed on the `target=` slot number, and therefore not on the
# whole `[ksys SYS_EXEC] ` prefix either (the slot sits between them): init's
# fork pool hands out 15 and 16 in alternation, and which one carries `hello`
# differs between the default and --no-default-features configs (15 stub-free,
# 16 with stubs). A marker naming a slot passes in one config and is vacuous in
# the other -- the slice-5.5 lesson, applied before it could bite. `entry=` is
# kept so this matches do_exec's trace and not some other line.
name=hello entry=

# The milestone itself: a C program compiled against a forked musl, exec'd out of
# the boot archive, reaching serial through printf -> VFS -> TTY.
#
# Two toolchains can produce it, and this log cannot tell them apart. The SDK
# flavor (P3c) is one `clang --target=aarch64-unknown-minixrs` call against
# $MINIXRS_SDK; the in-tree musl flavor (slice 5.6) compiles on the stand-in
# triple and links with rust-lld against target/musl-sysroot. The two binaries
# differ in size and segment count, but the markers below are BYTE-IDENTICAL
# across them -- same source, same libc, same ABI -- so nothing here needs to
# change per flavor, and equally nothing here can *prove* a flavor. That is what
# kernel/build.rs's host-side cargo::warning and the ELF checks in
# book/src/libc/overview.md are for.
#
# CI has no SDK, so qemu-smoke always exercises the musl flavor.
#
# This line does NOT prove the flush path, despite being the obvious candidate.
# musl's stdout starts *line* buffered (`.lbf = '\n'`), and it is __stdout_write
# -- reached on the first flush -- that sets f->lbf = -1 after the fork's ioctl
# answers -ENOTTY. So this write goes out immediately via the line-buffered
# path, and only the printfs AFTER it are fully buffered. The `iov ok` and
# `errno ok` markers below are the ones that reach the console solely because
# exit() ran __stdio_exit.
minix.rs hello: Hello from C!

# fd 2, unbuffered, through the same VFS path -- a different descriptor and a
# different buffering mode than the line above.
minix.rs hello: stderr works

# Phase-5 decision D7 (errno identity) proven at RUNTIME rather than only at
# compile time. tools/build-musl.sh statically asserts the POSIX magnitudes
# against the fork's own bits/errno.h; this checks the whole chain end to end --
# VFS answers EBADF for fd 3 (in range of the fd row, not open), the driver
# relays it, syscall_ret.c turns the negative return into errno, and the value C
# compares against <errno.h>'s EBADF matches. Emitted ONLY when write(3, ...)
# returns -1 *and* errno == EBADF, so it cannot appear by accident.
minix.rs hello: errno ok

# The two-iovec writev path. musl's __stdio_write hands writev the PENDING
# stream buffer as iov[0] and the new data as iov[1]; both are non-empty only
# when an over-large write arrives with bytes still buffered, which hello sets
# up deliberately. Without that setup every write in the program is a single
# iovec and a writev that ignored iov[1..] would pass unnoticed -- mutation-
# tested: looping only over iov[0] makes __stdio_write spin forever and takes
# all four lines below with it.
#
# Two independent halves, the 5.4 shape. The tail only reaches the console if
# the second iovec was sent...
iov-end
# ...and this says fwrite accounted for every byte. A writev that moved the
# bytes but under-reported would print the tail and still be broken.
minix.rs hello: iov ok match=1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slice 5.7: the BDEV band, the `memory` ramdisk driver, and the root image.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Every marker below is identical with and without `boot-stubs` AND with and
# without the musl sysroot. That is what the FIXED image size buys: in the
# sysroot-absent build `kernel/build.rs` packs the 15 KB `worker` ELF as `hello`,
# so a content-sized image would make len/pages/blocks config-dependent -- the
# slice-5.5/5.6 "right in one config, vacuous in the other" trap.

# The kernel copies the archive's `rootfs` blob into fresh RAM frames and maps
# them into the memory driver's address space, page by page. Every field is a
# constant (uspace::RAMDISK_VA, rootfs::ROOTFS_IMAGE_BYTES / _BLOCKS), so all
# three are asserted. Unlike the tty device page these are ordinary RAM mapped
# Prot::RW_DATA -- no `prot.device` carve-out is involved anywhere.
[ramdisk] mem va=0x80000000 len=1048576 pages=256

# The driver announces itself on the kernel debug channel, exactly like the six
# SEF servers and the tty driver.
[diag memory] sef ready

# ...and then proves the mapping is real, complete, and holds this build's image.
# Two 32-byte SYS_COPY(SELF -> SELF) reads, so the driver never dereferences the
# mapping and a page the kernel failed to map is an EFAULT return rather than an
# EL0 data abort.
#
# `blocks=256` cross-checks the image header's OWN block count against the length
# SYS_GETINFO(GET_RAMDISK) reported -- two independently derived numbers, binding
# mkfs's geometry to the kernel's copy.
#
# `tail=1` is the 32-byte label read from the image's LAST block, whose text
# deliberately differs from the header's. It is the only thing in the whole boot
# that proves the copy loop reached the end of the blob: a loop that failed to
# advance would map 256 pages of block 0 and pass every header check.
#
# This is a DEVICE-level check, not a format-level one -- no superblock is
# decoded and `minixrs-mfs` is not a dependency of this driver, so Phase 6 can
# drop virtio-blk in under an unchanged MFS. `tools/mkfs-mfs`'s round-trip test
# `the_image_header_agrees_with_the_real_superblock` is what licenses checking the
# header instead; slice 5.8's READSUPER closes it for real.
[diag memory] ramdisk ok blocks=256 tail=1

# VFS drives the block device over BDEV_READ, resolving `memory` through DS
# rather than hard-coding boot_endpoint(MEM_PROC_NR) -- the 5.3 contract, with the
# same non-deterministic-publish caveat and the same distinguishable
# `bdev.ds FAIL` fallback.
[diag vfs] bdev.ds ok ep=

# A real read. The reply *is* the byte count, so a driver replying OK gives a
# different number here. This is also the first SUCCESSFUL `SAFECOPY_TO` anywhere
# in the tree -- every other use is a denial probe -- so it is what proves the
# kernel's CPF_WRITE + Prot::writable success path at all.
[diag vfs] bdev.read ok n=32

# The header bytes survived IPC + grant + safecopy...
[diag vfs] bdev.head ok match=1

# ...and the `block` field reached the right page. Head and tail do NOT subsume
# each other: a driver that ignored `block` would return the header for both, and
# the driver's own `tail=1` above proves the kernel's copy loop, not BDEV
# indexing. VFS zeroes its buffer between the two reads, so a read that moved
# nothing cannot pass this on stale bytes.
[diag vfs] bdev.tail ok match=1

# Ten refusals, each well-formed but for one field: minor 7 (-> ENXIO, the
# driver's own minor check), one block past the end (-> EINVAL, not EIO: a block
# device's size is known to its client), BDEV_MAX_IO + 1 bytes (-> EINVAL, the
# deliberate departure from CDEV's clamp -- a short block read is useless to a
# filesystem), a negative length (-> EINVAL, which unchecked would widen into a
# ~16 EiB u64), a grant issued to PM (-> EPERM, the kernel's `who_to` check), a
# CPF_READ-only grant used as a copy DESTINATION (-> EPERM: the access mask in the
# WRITE direction, which slice 5.3 never exercised), BDEV_WRITE (-> EROFS, not
# ENOSYS -- that distinction is the whole reason the request has a number),
# BDEV_WRITE to minor 7 (-> ENXIO, not EROFS: the driver validates before it
# refuses, so it never asserts read-onlyness about a device it does not have --
# and without this probe that arm could be reduced back to a bare EROFS with no
# marker moving), a request one past the band (-> ENOSYS, and the reply itself is
# the assertion: a dropped unknown would block VFS in its SENDREC forever and take
# every later marker with it), and SYS_GETINFO(GET_RAMDISK) issued by VFS
# (-> EPERM, the gate that keeps a VA mapped into one address space from being
# handed to another). A missing check makes its probe succeed and turns this into
# `bdev.deny FAIL <name>`.
[diag vfs] bdev.deny ok n=10

# Coverage produced by `cargo llvm-cov --lcov` in the coverage CI job.
sonar.rust.lcov.reportPaths=lcov.info

# Coverage exclusions: IPC glue that traps into the kernel cannot execute under
# a host `cargo test` — it is verified instead by the QEMU boot trace
# (kernel-side `[ipc]`/`[ksys]`/`[pf]` lines), the same integration-only path
# that already excludes `**/*.S` from analysis. Three kinds:
#   * `servers/**/src/main.rs`, `drivers/**/src/main.rs`,

#     dispatching to handlers that SEND/SENDREC via SVC, or a plain user program
#     like the slice-4.7 exec target `userland/worker` (getpid loop + exit).
#   * `minixrs-ipc/src/**` — the syscall trap library itself (SVC/SYSCALL asm
#     stubs); every function either is inline asm or an off-target `unreachable!`
#     fallback, so nothing here is host-executable.
#   * `server-rt/src/sef.rs` — the SEF startup handshake + receive loop,
#     `server-rt/src/ds.rs` — the `sef_publish_to_ds` / `sef_retrieve_from_ds`
#     helpers, `server-rt/src/diag.rs` — the `diag_print` / `diag_fmt`
#     kernel-debug-channel helpers (slice 5.1), `server-rt/src/grant.rs` — the
#     `GrantPool` grant-table client (slice 5.2), and `server-rt/src/kcall.rs` —
#     the `SYS_SAFECOPY` / `SYS_COPY` clients lifted out of PM (slice 5.3), all of
#     which SENDREC/RECEIVE/NOTIFY via `minixrs-ipc`.
#   * `drivers/tty/src/pl011.rs` — volatile MMIO stores to the UART's data and
#     flag registers (slice 5.3). Not IPC, but the same category: the registers
#     only exist at the device VA the kernel pre-maps into TTY's address space, so
#     nothing here can run under a host `cargo test`. It is verified by the
#     `minix.rs console: tty online (EL0)` boot marker — the one line in the log
#     with no kernel trace prefix. Listed explicitly because the
#     `drivers/**/src/main.rs` glob does not reach a sibling module.
#   * `tools/**/src/main.rs` — host build-tool entry points (`tools/gen-c-headers`,
#     slice 5.0): argv parsing plus `create_dir_all`/`write` of artifacts whose
#     *content* is produced by the crate's measured library modules and unit
#     tested there. The I/O shell is verified end to end by the CI `c-headers`
#     job, which regenerates the headers and compiles them with
#     `clang -std=c11 -fsyntax-only`.
# Testable logic stays in measured submodules — e.g. `servers/vm/src/region.rs`,
# `servers/ds/src/registry.rs` (the DS name→endpoint store),
# `drivers/tty/src/cdev.rs` (the pure `CDEV_WRITE` parse/validate), and
# `server-rt/src/classify.rs` + `server-rt/src/payload.rs` (the SEF message
# classifier and the payload scalar accessors), which carry the host unit tests.
# Where a trap module has pure logic worth testing but is too small to split
# (`diag.rs`'s chunk arithmetic, `grant.rs`'s allocate/revoke helpers), the tests
# still run under `cargo test` — exclusion suppresses *measurement*, not execution.

# Coverage exclusions: IPC glue that traps into the kernel cannot execute under
# a host `cargo test` — it is verified instead by the QEMU boot trace
# (kernel-side `[ipc]`/`[ksys]`/`[pf]` lines), the same integration-only path
# that already excludes `**/*.S` from analysis. Three kinds:
#   * `servers/**/src/main.rs`, `drivers/**/src/main.rs`,
#     `userland/**/src/main.rs` — freestanding entry points: a RECEIVE loop
#     dispatching to handlers that SEND/SENDREC via SVC, or a plain user program
#     like the slice-4.7 exec target `userland/worker` (getpid loop + exit).
#   * `minixrs-ipc/src/**` — the syscall trap library itself (SVC/SYSCALL asm
#     stubs); every function either is inline asm or an off-target `unreachable!`
#     fallback, so nothing here is host-executable.
#   * `server-rt/src/sef.rs` — the SEF startup handshake + receive loop,
#     `server-rt/src/ds.rs` — the `sef_publish_to_ds` / `sef_retrieve_from_ds`
#     helpers, `server-rt/src/diag.rs` — the `diag_print` / `diag_fmt`
#     kernel-debug-channel helpers (slice 5.1), `server-rt/src/grant.rs` — the
#     `GrantPool` grant-table client (slice 5.2), and `server-rt/src/kcall.rs` —
#     the `SYS_SAFECOPY` / `SYS_COPY` clients lifted out of PM (slice 5.3), all of
#     which SENDREC/RECEIVE/NOTIFY via `minixrs-ipc`.
#   * `drivers/tty/src/pl011.rs` — volatile MMIO stores to the UART's data and
#     flag registers (slice 5.3). Not IPC, but the same category: the registers
#     only exist at the device VA the kernel pre-maps into TTY's address space, so
#     nothing here can run under a host `cargo test`. It is verified by the
#     `minix.rs console: tty online (EL0)` boot marker — the one line in the log
#     with no kernel trace prefix. Listed explicitly because the
#     `drivers/**/src/main.rs` glob does not reach a sibling module.
#   * `tools/**/src/main.rs` — host build-tool entry points (`tools/gen-c-headers`,
#     slice 5.0): argv parsing plus `create_dir_all`/`write` of artifacts whose
#     *content* is produced by the crate's measured library modules and unit
#     tested there. The I/O shell is verified end to end by the CI `c-headers`
#     job, which regenerates the headers and compiles them with
#     `clang -std=c11 -fsyntax-only`.
# Testable logic stays in measured submodules — e.g. `servers/vm/src/region.rs`,
# `servers/ds/src/registry.rs` (the DS name→endpoint store),
# `drivers/tty/src/cdev.rs` (the pure `CDEV_WRITE` parse/validate), and
# `server-rt/src/classify.rs` + `server-rt/src/payload.rs` (the SEF message
# classifier and the payload scalar accessors), which carry the host unit tests.
# Where a trap module has pure logic worth testing but is too small to split
# (`diag.rs`'s chunk arithmetic, `grant.rs`'s allocate/revoke helpers), the tests
# still run under `cargo test` — exclusion suppresses *measurement*, not execution.
sonar.coverage.exclusions=servers/**/src/main.rs,drivers/**/src/main.rs,userland/**/src/main.rs,minixrs-ipc/src/**,server-rt/src/sef.rs,server-rt/src/ds.rs,server-rt/src/diag.rs,server-rt/src/grant.rs,server-rt/src/kcall.rs,drivers/tty/src/pl011.rs,tools/**/src/main.rs

+// file-system server, MFS being the first and only one (slice 5.8).
+// Like the PM/VFS/BDEV/CDEV/VM/DS/SEF/SCHED ranges these are *server IPC
+// requests*, not kernel calls. `0x900` was reserved for this band when VFS took
+// `0x800` and BDEV `0xA00`, so it slots in between them and the numeric ordering
+// the whole scheme rests on is preserved. Numbering is minix.rs-specific — MINIX
+// 3 carries its VFS↔FS protocol in `include/minix/vfsif.h` with a far larger
+// request set (PUTNODE, STAT, GETDENTS, the whole write path), none of which
+// minix.rs inherits: this band is exactly the three requests a read-only open →
+// read → close needs, on the `CDEV_READ` precedent that a request absent until it
+// has a consumer is better than a request stubbed out.

+// not by grant. It is control plane, not the data path D4 provisioned grants
+// for — the same call the `PM_EXEC` name and the `DS_PUBLISH` key already make.
+// It costs the FS server no staging buffer, which is its scarcest resource (one
+// page of stack, all of it already spoken for by the block buffer), and it
+// deletes the confused-deputy question outright, because there is no granter to
+// name. The cost is the cap: a path longer than [`FS_PATH_MAX`] is
+// `ENAMETOOLONG`, refused by VFS before it reaches the wire.

+// remaining tail each round rather than advancing an offset.

+/// no filesystem this build reads, `EIO` for a device that could not be read).
+/// On success the reply payload carries the root inode number in
+/// [`FS_SUPER_BLOCK_SIZE_OFF`]`..+4` (i32), and its size in blocks in
+/// Those three are what make the reply worth having: a client that only wanted
+/// "did it mount" would take the `m_type`. They are the numbers a boot marker can
+/// cross-check against the *device*'s independently derived geometry.
+/// VFS → FS: resolve an absolute path to an inode.

+/// Reply `m_type` is `OK` or a negative errno — `ENOENT` for a component that
+/// does not exist, `ENOTDIR` for an intermediate component that is not a
+/// directory, `ENAMETOOLONG` for a path that fills the field with no NUL,
+/// `EINVAL` for a relative path, `ENODEV` if nothing is mounted. On success the
+/// reply carries the inode number in [`FS_INO_OFF`]`..+4` (i32), the inode's mode
+/// in [`FS_MODE_OFF`]`..+4` (i32, widened from MinixFS's `u16`), and its size in
+/// Mode and size ride along so there is **no separate stat request**: the two
+/// facts a client needs before reading — is this a directory, and how big is it —
+/// are exactly what a lookup already had to decode.
+/// VFS → FS: read from an inode into the client's granted buffer.
+/// Payload: the inode number in [`FS_INO_OFF`]`..+4` (i32), the grant id in

[package]
name = "minixrs-mfs"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
license = "BSD-3-Clause"
publish = false

# The MFS *server* (slice 5.8). Gated behind a `server` feature so the format
# library stays a one-dependency crate that `kernel/build.rs` can pull into its
# build-script graph (via the `tools/mkfs-mfs` build-dependency) for free.
#
# **The cost of that gate, stated where someone will read it: this binary is
# invisible to every CI job.** `clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `miri`, and
# `cargo llvm-cov` all run without `--features server`, so a `required-features`
# target is silently skipped. Three things hold the line:
#
#   1. Every line with a decision in it lives in the **lib** (`proto.rs`,
#      `walk.rs`) — the bin is SEF/IPC/grant/diag glue and nothing else, the
#      `servers/ds` `registry.rs`/`main.rs` split taken further than usual.
#   2. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs one extra step,
#      `cargo clippy -p minixrs-mfs --features server --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
#   3. The QEMU boot smoke test builds it for real, because `kernel/build.rs`
#      threads `--features server` through the nested build (the same mechanism
#      that threads PM's `--no-default-features`).
#
# `name` is mandatory and must equal the package name: `build_server` in
# `kernel/build.rs` looks the ELF up by that basename.
[[bin]]
name = "minixrs-mfs"
path = "src/main.rs"
required-features = ["server"]

[features]
# Everything the server half needs. Off by default so the format library — which
# `kernel/build.rs` reaches at build-script time — costs the kernel build nothing.
server = ["dep:minixrs-ipc", "dep:minixrs-server-rt", "dep:minixrs-abi-note"]

# `MFS_BLOCK_SIZE == BDEV_BLOCK_SIZE` against it, and it is already in the
# kernel's build-script graph.

minixrs-server-rt = { path = "../../server-rt", optional = true }
minixrs-abi-note = { path = "../../minixrs-abi-note", optional = true }

[lints]
workspace = true

input.old_string:
# VFS drives the block device over BDEV_READ, resolving `memory` through DS
# rather than hard-coding boot_endpoint(MEM_PROC_NR) -- the 5.3 contract, with the
# same non-deterministic-publish caveat and the same distinguishable
# `bdev.ds FAIL` fallback.
[diag vfs] bdev.ds ok ep=

# A real read. The reply *is* the byte count, so a driver replying OK gives a
# different number here. This is also the first SUCCESSFUL `SAFECOPY_TO` anywhere
# in the tree -- every other use is a denial probe -- so it is what proves the
# kernel's CPF_WRITE + Prot::writable success path at all.
[diag vfs] bdev.read ok n=32

# The header bytes survived IPC + grant + safecopy...
[diag vfs] bdev.head ok match=1

# ...and the `block` field reached the right page. Head and tail do NOT subsume
# each other: a driver that ignored `block` would return the header for both, and
# the driver's own `tail=1` above proves the kernel's copy loop, not BDEV
# indexing. VFS zeroes its buffer between the two reads, so a read that moved
# nothing cannot pass this on stale bytes.
[diag vfs] bdev.tail ok match=1

# Ten refusals, each well-formed but for one field: minor 7 (-> ENXIO, the
# driver's own minor check), one block past the end (-> EINVAL, not EIO: a block
# device's size is known to its client), BDEV_MAX_IO + 1 bytes (-> EINVAL, the
# deliberate departure from CDEV's clamp -- a short block read is useless to a
# filesystem), a negative length (-> EINVAL, which unchecked would widen into a
# ~16 EiB u64), a grant issued to PM (-> EPERM, the kernel's `who_to` check), a
# CPF_READ-only grant used as a copy DESTINATION (-> EPERM: the access mask in the
# WRITE direction, which slice 5.3 never exercised), BDEV_WRITE (-> EROFS, not

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! Path traversal and read policy, allocator-free (slice 5.8).
4	//!
5	//! This is the `Vec`-free rewrite of `tools/mkfs-mfs`'s `verify.rs`, which is the
6	//! reference implementation: same decoders, same zone resolver, same directory
7	//! walk, with `block()` replaced by a `BDEV_READ`. The structure is deliberately
8	//! mirrored so the two can be diffed, and the `fs.selfcheck` boot marker is the
9	//! one place the two readers meet over a real image.
10	//!
11	//! Two of `verify.rs`'s functions could not survive the move to `no_std`:
12	//!
13	//!   * `read_inode_bytes` materializes a whole directory into a `Vec`. The server
14	//!     has one 4 KiB block buffer and a one-page stack, so it **streams** instead —
15	//!     one block at a time, asking [`find_in_block`] about each. That is why this
16	//!     module offers a per-block search rather than a directory reader.
17	//!   * `read_dir` is absent entirely. Nothing needs it: there is no `GETDENTS`
18	//!     request, on the `CDEV_READ` precedent that a request without a consumer is
19	//!     better absent than stubbed.
20	//!
21	//! ## Every bound here exists to stop a loop
22	//!
23	//! The server's loop bounds all come from the *device*, and a corrupt image is
24	//! not a hypothetical the way it is for a filesystem with an `fsck`: a directory

26	//! MFS blocks VFS, which blocks init, which takes the slice-5.4-to-5.6 markers

44	/// must not have, and "I cannot read this" is the honest alternative.

48	#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]

51	    /// only way a client learns where a file ends, since no size is cached

58	}

61	///
62	/// The three ways a path can be malformed, in the order a caller should hear
63	/// about them:

65	/// 1. Empty, or not starting with `/` → `EINVAL`. There is no working directory
66	///    on minix.rs and no `chdir`, so a relative path is not a thing that could be
67	///    resolved — it is a malformed request, not a missing file.
68	/// 2. A component longer than [`NAME_MAX`] → `ENAMETOOLONG`. MinixFS cannot
69	///    *store* such a name, so no image can contain one and `ENOENT` would be a
70	///    less informative way of saying the same thing.
71	/// 3. Otherwise the path itself, unchanged.

81	        if component.len() > NAME_MAX {

83	        }
84	    }
85	    Ok(path)

89	///
90	/// Repeated and trailing slashes collapse — `/etc//motd/` walks the same two

92	/// yields nothing at all, so it resolves to the root inode without a single
93	/// directory read.
94	pub fn components(path: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
95	    path.split('/').filter(|c| !c.is_empty())
96	}
97	
98	/// Find `name` among the directory entries of one fetched block.
99	///
100	/// **Returns the inode number by value**, so the caller's borrow of the block
101	/// buffer ends at the call. That is not a style preference: the buffer is a
102	/// single shared staging area, and the next thing the caller does is fetch the

105	///

git commit --signoff -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat: MFS server + the FS band at 0x900 (slice 5.8a)

The first file system in minix.rs. Slice 5.7 built everything under it — the
compile-time MinixFS v3 image, the `memory` ramdisk driver, and the `fs/mfs`
format library — but `fs/mfs/src/main.rs` was a five-line placeholder and band
`0x900` was still reserved. This lands both.

**The FS band** (`kernel-shared/src/callnr.rs`, between VFS and BDEV):
`FS_READSUPER` + `FS_LOOKUP` + `FS_READ`, and nothing else. No PUTNODE (MFS keeps
no per-open state — there is no node to put), no stat (`FS_LOOKUP`'s reply already
carries mode and size), no GETDENTS (no consumer) — the `CDEV_READ` precedent that
a request without a consumer is better absent than stubbed.

Two shapes travel there. The **path is inline**, NUL-padded to `FS_PATH_MAX`: it
is control plane rather than the data path grants were provisioned for (the
`PM_EXEC` name and `DS_PUBLISH` key make the same call), it costs the server no
staging buffer, and it deletes the confused-deputy question outright because
there is no granter to name. The **data travels by grant**, with no granter field
and no grant-offset field, the 5.2/5.3/5.7 rule verbatim. An over-long `FS_READ`
is **clamped, not `EINVAL`** — the deliberate departure back towards `CDEV_WRITE`:
BDEV refuses because a filesystem cannot interpret half a block, but here the
client is VFS, whose job is hiding staging from POSIX, and a short read is what
`read()` means.

`0x900` was the last reserved slot, so `0x700..0xC00` is now fully allocated. The
test that recorded it as free is replaced by one recording that it is not.

**The server** (`fs/mfs`, packed between `memory` and `vfs`). Every line with a
decision in it is in the *library* — `proto.rs` (wire codec) and `walk.rs`
(traversal and read policy, the `Vec`-free rewrite of `mkfs-mfs`'s `verify.rs`) —
because `[[bin]] required-features = ["server"]` makes the binary invisible to
clippy, miri, and llvm-cov alike. Mitigated three ways: the lib-heavy split, one
extra CI clippy step, and a note in `Cargo.toml`.

The 4 KiB block buffer cannot be a `main`-frame local — a server stack is exactly
one page — so it is a `.bss` static reached only through a `Blocks` capability
token whose `read(&mut self) -> &[u8; N]` makes "hold a directory block across the
next fetch" a borrow-check error rather than a promise. `SERVER_STACK_BYTES` is
new in `uspace` purely to carry the tripwire for that, and the kernel now
const-asserts its own stack mapping against it.

`kernel_shared::rootfs` gains the image's *contents* (`ROOTFS_MOTD`,
`ROOTFS_PATTERN_*`, the paths), so `build_rootfs` loses its literals and the
server's read proof is a check rather than a transcription.

VFS's `bdev_demo`/`bdev_denials` retire: MFS is the real block-device client now,
so the refusal battery moves there verbatim and VFS goes back to knowing nothing
about block devices.

Proof, all self-driving from MFS's own prologue: `[as] mfs nr=6`,
`[diag mfs] sef ready`, `bdev.ds ok ep=`, `mount ok root=1 bs=4096 blocks=256`
(cross-checking the superblock's `s_zones` against the driver's header-derived
count), `fs.selfcheck ok n=31 match=1` (the whole reader over the real image,
byte-compared against `ROOTFS_MOTD`), `fs.indirect ok match=1` (`/etc/pattern` at
offset 7*4096 — the only marker that reaches the single-indirect arm, and why 5.7
made that file mandatory), `bdev.tail ok match=1`, `bdev.deny ok n=10`.
`bdev.read`/`bdev.head` retire, strictly subsumed by `mount ok`.

Both feature configs boot green; all 75 markers pass.
EOF

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! minix.rs VFS (virtual file system) server — the POSIX write path (slice 5.4),
4	//! plus the grant and console demos slices 5.2 and 5.3 left behind as regression
5	//! probes.
6	//!
7	//! Slice 4.2 stood VFS up as a real boot server: it boots through the SEF
8	//! framework and publishes its endpoint to DS. Slice 5.2 gave it the granting half
9	//! of the first cross-address-space copy ([`grant_test`]), and 5.3 made it the
10	//! first client of the TTY console driver ([`tty_demo`]).
11	//!
12	//! Slice 5.4 makes it a *file system* server, in the one sense that matters at
13	//! this stage: an ordinary user process can now write to a descriptor. See
14	//! [`do_write`].
15	//!
16	//! ## The write path, and its one copy
17	//!
18	//! ```text
19	//! user ──VFS_WRITE{fd,buf,len}──► VFS ──CDEV_WRITE{minor,gid,len,off}──► TTY
20	//!                                  │                                      │
21	//!                                  └── magic grant: caller's buf ──────────┘
22	//!                                          (kernel copies, once)
23	//! ```
24	//!
25	//! VFS resolves the descriptor, issues a **magic** (third-party) grant naming the
26	//! *caller's* buffer with the driver as grantee, and forwards the id. TTY then
27	//! safecopies straight out of the caller's address space into its staging buffer.
28	//! The bytes never pass through VFS — there is exactly one copy, from the process
29	//! that wrote them to the driver that transmits them, which is the whole point of
30	//! the D4 grant design.
31	//!
32	//! Three properties hold that path together, each of which has its own probe in
33	//! the boot log:
34	//!
35	//! **The grant's owner is the kernel-stamped `m_source`.** VFS holds `SYS_PROC`,
36	//! which is what makes a magic grant legal for it at all; a caller-supplied owner
37	//! field would therefore let *any* VFS client aim a privileged cross-address-space
38	//! copy at a third party's memory. `VFS_WRITE` has no such field. This is slice
39	//! 5.2/5.3's confused-deputy rule applied to the granting side.
40	//!
41	//! **VFS absorbs short writes.** `CDEV_MAX_IO` is a driver staging detail; a
42	//! `write()` return value is not allowed to expose it. So [`write_all`] re-sends
43	//! with `offset` advanced until the buffer is out and reports the total.
44	//!
45	//! **Every request gets a reply.** VFS's clients are all inside a SENDREC, so a
46	//! dropped message blocks the caller forever — TTY's rule, and now VFS's.
47	//!
48	//! ## What slice 5.8 took away
49	//!
50	//! Slice 5.7's `bdev_demo` / `bdev_denials` are **gone**. They existed because
51	//! there was no other client for the block device and no successful `SAFECOPY_TO`
52	//! anywhere in the tree; MFS is now the real client, so the whole battery moved
53	//! there verbatim (`bdev.ds` / `bdev.tail` / `bdev.deny` are `[diag mfs]` lines
54	//! now). With them go VFS's `rootfs::*` / `BDEV_*` / `GET_RAMDISK` imports: VFS is
55	//! back to knowing nothing about block devices, which is the layering the FS band
56	//! exists to create.
57	//!
58	//! Built as a freestanding aarch64 ELF (see `servers/vfs/user.ld`), packed into
59	//! the kernel's boot-image archive by `kernel/build.rs`, and loaded into its own
60	//! per-process AddrSpace at boot by `arch::aarch64::userland::load_boot_server`.
61	
62	// Freestanding for the real (bare-metal) build, but a normal host binary under
63	// `cargo test` (no host tests yet — the SEF/IPC glue is QEMU-verified). The

3	//! minix.rs `init` — PID 1, the first user process (slice 4.8).
4	//!
5	//! Unlike the demo stubs it replaces, `init` is a real boot module: it is packed
6	//! into the boot-image archive with its true proc number (`INIT_PROC_NR = 10`)
7	//! and loaded + made runnable by the ordinary boot loop
8	//! (`kernel/src/arch/aarch64/userland.rs`), not hand-released by PM. It runs as
9	//! an ordinary user process — the shared `USER_PRIV_ID` privilege (SENDREC to PM
10	//! and VFS, and no kernel calls at all) — so the whole process lifecycle flows
11	//! through PM, and every byte of output through VFS, in the POSIX shape
12	//! (user → server, never user → kernel).
13	//!
14	//! `init` is the live exercise for the Phase-4 process machinery that the
15	//! slice-4.6/4.7 stub E demonstrated: it forks a child, the child execs a
16	//! boot-image binary, and the parent `wait`s to reap the zombie before looping
17	//! to fork again. Each cycle recycles the same fork-pool slot with an advancing
18	//! endpoint generation — observable in the boot trace as `SYS_FORK` /
19	//! `SYS_EXEC` / `SYS_EXIT` triples.
20	//!
21	//! Slice 5.6 makes the exec target the *caller's* choice — `PM_EXEC` carries a
22	//! name now, instead of PM hardcoding one — and init alternates between
23	//! [`EXEC_TARGETS`]: `worker` (5.5's exec-stack probe) and `hello` (the first C
24	//! program on minix.rs). Alternating keeps both proofs live; switching outright
25	//! would have retired the exec-ABI markers to make room for the C ones.
26	//!
27	//! Slice 5.4 gives it a voice. Before the fork loop it writes to **fd 1 and fd
28	//! 2** through VFS, which grants the buffer on to the TTY driver — the POSIX
29	//! write path, end to end, from an ordinary user process. init has no debug
30	//! channel of its own (`SYS_DIAGCTL` is a kernel call, and a user proc holds
31	//! none), so it reports *through the path under test*: if the path regresses the
32	//! lines change or vanish, and the boot markers go with them. See [`announce`].
33	//!
34	//! Slice 5.5 gives it one more thing to say. `SYS_EXEC` now hands a new image a
35	//! SysV initial stack, and `worker` checks that frame against its own `sp` and
36	//! encodes the verdict as its exit status — so init, which reaps it anyway,
37	//! prints the **first** such status and nothing thereafter. See

3	//! minix.rs VFS (virtual file system) server — the POSIX write path (slice 5.4)
4	//! and read path (5.8), plus the grant and console demos slices 5.2 and 5.3 left
5	//! behind as regression probes.
6	//!
7	//! Slice 4.2 stood VFS up as a real boot server: it boots through the SEF
8	//! framework and publishes its endpoint to DS. Slice 5.2 gave it the granting half
9	//! of the first cross-address-space copy ([`grant_test`]), and 5.3 made it the
10	//! first client of the TTY console driver ([`tty_demo`]).
11	//!
12	//! Slice 5.4 makes it a *file system* server, in the one sense that matters at
13	//! this stage: an ordinary user process can now write to a descriptor. See
14	//! [`do_write`]. Slice 5.8 gives it something to read — a real filesystem behind
15	//! [`do_open`] / [`do_read`] / [`do_close`], served by MFS.
16	//!
17	//! ## The write path, and its one copy
18	//!
19	//! ```text
20	//! user ──VFS_WRITE{fd,buf,len}──► VFS ──CDEV_WRITE{minor,gid,len,off}──► TTY
21	//!                                  │                                      │
22	//!                                  └── magic grant: caller's buf ──────────┘
23	//!                                          (kernel copies, once)
24	//! ```
25	//!
26	//! VFS resolves the descriptor, issues a **magic** (third-party) grant naming the
27	//! *caller's* buffer with the driver as grantee, and forwards the id. TTY then
28	//! safecopies straight out of the caller's address space into its staging buffer.
29	//! The bytes never pass through VFS — there is exactly one copy, from the process
30	//! that wrote them to the driver that transmits them, which is the whole point of
31	//! the D4 grant design.
32	//!
33	//! Three properties hold that path together, each of which has its own probe in
34	//! the boot log:
35	//!
36	//! **The grant's owner is the kernel-stamped `m_source`.** VFS holds `SYS_PROC`,
37	//! which is what makes a magic grant legal for it at all; a caller-supplied owner
38	//! field would therefore let *any* VFS client aim a privileged cross-address-space
39	//! copy at a third party's memory. `VFS_WRITE` has no such field. This is slice
40	//! 5.2/5.3's confused-deputy rule applied to the granting side.
41	//!
42	//! **VFS absorbs short writes.** `CDEV_MAX_IO` is a driver staging detail; a
43	//! `write()` return value is not allowed to expose it. So [`write_all`] re-sends
44	//! with `offset` advanced until the buffer is out and reports the total.
45	//!
46	//! **Every request gets a reply.** VFS's clients are all inside a SENDREC, so a
47	//! dropped message blocks the caller forever — TTY's rule, and now VFS's.
48	//!
49	//! ## The read path, and its two copies
50	//!
51	//! ```text
52	//! user ──VFS_OPEN{path,len}───► VFS ──SYS_COPY──────────► (the path, into VFS)
53	//!                                │
54	//!                                └──FS_LOOKUP{path}─────► MFS  → (ino, mode)
55	//!
56	//! user ──VFS_READ{fd,buf,len}──► VFS ──FS_READ{ino,gid,len,pos}──► MFS
57	//!                                 │                                 │
58	//!                                 └── magic grant: caller's buf ────┘
59	//! ```
60	//!
61	//! **Two copies, not one**, and the difference from the write path above is
62	//! deliberate: MFS stages a block through its own buffer (device → MFS) before
63	//! safecopying the requested slice out of it (MFS → caller). A MinixFS read is
64	//! rarely block-aligned in both the file and the destination, and a *hole* has no
65	//! device block to copy from at all — so the staging cannot be elided, and this is
66	//! MINIX 3's own shape. Only the second copy is VFS's grant; the bytes still never
67	//! pass through VFS.
68	//!
69	//! **`SYS_COPY` reads the path, and its source is the kernel-stamped `m_source`.**
70	//! `SYS_COPY` has no per-target authorization whatsoever, so a payload-supplied
71	//! source would let any client read any process's memory through VFS. This is the
72	//! same confused-deputy rule as the granting side, in its sharpest form.
73	//!
74	//! **VFS does not loop on read.** It loops on `write` because a driver's staging
75	//! limit may not reach `write()`'s return value; `read()` is explicitly allowed to
76	//! return less than asked for, and a file read is short at EOF regardless.
77	//!
78	//! ## What slice 5.8 took away

80	//! Slice 5.7's `bdev_demo` / `bdev_denials` are **gone**. They existed because
81	//! there was no other client for the block device and no successful `SAFECOPY_TO`
82	//! anywhere in the tree; MFS is now the real client, so the whole battery moved
83	//! there verbatim (`bdev.ds` / `bdev.tail` / `bdev.deny` are `[diag mfs]` lines
84	//! now). With them go VFS's `rootfs::*` / `BDEV_*` / `GET_RAMDISK` imports: VFS is
85	//! back to knowing nothing about block devices, which is the layering the FS band
86	//! exists to create.
87	//!

90	//! per-process AddrSpace at boot by `arch::aarch64::userland::load_boot_server`.

1	# tests/qemu-boot.expected -- required substrings for a healthy QEMU boot log.
2	# One literal substring per line; blank lines and '#' comments are ignored.
3	# Checked by tools/check-boot-log.sh via `grep -aF` (the log interleaves raw
4	# single-char tick bytes, so it must be forced to text). Substrings stop just
5	# before the first run-variable field (ttbr0_pa / child_e / entry / freed / at);
6	# nr= values are fixed boot-table slots (kernel-shared/src/com.rs).
7	
8	# Kernel banner (kernel/src/main.rs)
9	minix.rs booting on aarch64
10	
11	# Address-space bring-up: 10 servers + init (arch/aarch64/userland.rs). The tty
12	# line is new in slice 5.3, the memory line in 5.7, and the mfs line in 5.8.
13	#
14	# The order below is `kernel/build.rs`'s `servers` array, and it is load-bearing
15	# rather than cosmetic: DS first so every later DS_PUBLISH lands, then each
16	# server before its first client's DS_RETRIEVE -- ds < tty < memory < mfs < vfs.
17	# MEM precedes MFS (MFS's `bdev.ds` lookup) and MFS precedes VFS (VFS's `fs.ds`
18	# lookup). Both lookups fall back to boot_endpoint and say so, so a reordering
19	# turns those two markers red rather than hanging the boot.
20	[as] vm nr=7 ttbr0_pa=
21	[as] ds nr=5 ttbr0_pa=
22	[as] tty nr=4 ttbr0_pa=
23	[as] memory nr=3 ttbr0_pa=
24	[as] mfs nr=6 ttbr0_pa=
25	[as] vfs nr=1 ttbr0_pa=
26	[as] sched nr=9 ttbr0_pa=
27	[as] rs nr=2 ttbr0_pa=
28	[as] pm nr=0 ttbr0_pa=
29	[as] init nr=10 ttbr0_pa=
30	
31	# ...plus the 4 boot stubs (14 [as] lines total)
32	[as] stub A nr=11 ttbr0_pa=
33	[as] stub B nr=12 ttbr0_pa=
34	[as] stub C nr=13 ttbr0_pa=
35	[as] stub D nr=14 ttbr0_pa=
36	
37	# init's fork/exec/wait cycle (head-carved kernel traces; slot 15 is the
38	# fork-pool base, recycled every cycle; exec renames the child to "worker")
39	[ksys SYS_FORK] parent=i nr=10 child_nr=15
40	[ksys SYS_EXEC] target=15 name=worker entry=
41	[ksys SYS_EXIT] target=w nr=15 freed=
42	
43	# Stub D's designed SIGSEGV chain: page fault -> VM -> SYS_KILL sig=11 -> PM
44	# tears the stub down with SYS_EXIT
45	[pf] proc=D far=
46	[ksys SYS_KILL] target=D nr=14 sig=11 -> pm
47	[ksys SYS_EXIT] target=D nr=14 freed=
48	
49	# RS's periodic kernel alarm: assert only the FIRST fire (always inside the
50	# head carve-out) -- timing-robust under slow CI TCG, unlike a fire count
51	[alarm 1] owner=r nr=2 at=
52	
53	# Slice 5.1: stub A's one-shot bad-pointer probes. Each returns EFAULT instead
54	# of taking an EL1 data abort (which the forbidden list catches as a panic).
55	# Between them they cover every arm of the copy engine: probe 1 is a fully
56	# unmapped page, probe 2 straddles A's stack page into the unmapped one above
57	# it, probe 3 fails in the deferred MF_DELIVERMSG flush and lands EFAULT in A's
58	# parked x0, and probe 4 names A's *mapped but read-only* code page -- the only
59	# check on that path is the copy engine's own Prot::writable test, since the
60	# kernel writes through the HHDM alias where EL0 permission bits do not apply.
61	# call=1 is SEND; nr=11 is stub A. These lines are unsampled, so unlike
62	# `[ipc N]` they cannot drift with IPC ordering.
63	[efault] proc=A nr=11 call=1 va=0x900000
64	[efault] proc=A nr=11 call=1 va=0x800ff8
65	[efault deliver] proc=A nr=11 va=0x900000
66	[efault deliver] proc=A nr=11 va=0x400000

71	# the six: vm is the first server packed in the MXBI archive, pm the last, so
72	# together they bracket the whole roster.
73	[diag vm] sef ready
74	[diag pm] sef ready

77	# read-only buffer and hands the id over in a PM_GRANT_TEST message; PM reads it
78	# through the grant, then reads the *same* bytes again with the ungranted

84	[ksys SYS_SAFECOPY] granter=

16	## Where servers live
17	
18	Servers are freestanding `#![no_std]` / `#![no_main]` ELF binaries linked with
19	their own `user.ld` (page-aligned segments based at `0x0010_0000`) and branded
20	with the minixrs ELF identity note, which the kernel requires of every image it
21	loads. The kernel's `build.rs` compiles each for the `aarch64-unknown-minixrs`
22	target and concatenates them into a single **MXBI archive** embedded in the
23	kernel image; the boot loader
24	(`kernel/src/arch/aarch64/userland.rs`) walks the archive and loads each module
25	into the proc slot named by its record. Each server gets its own per-process
26	TTBR0, so they all share the same low load base with no collision.
27	
28	A server has no `println`. Its behaviour is observed through kernel-side traces
29	(`[ipc]`, `[ksys]`, `[pf]`, `[alarm]`), and since slice 5.1 it can also emit a
30	line itself through the kernel debug channel — `server-rt`'s `diag_print` /
31	`diag_fmt` issue a `SYS_DIAGCTL` carrying the text inline, which the kernel prints
32	prefixed with the caller's own name (`[diag vfs] …`). That is deliberately a
33	*debug* channel, not stdio: it exists to keep working while stdio itself is under
34	construction. Real console output arrives via the TTY driver (see
35	[Drivers](../drivers/overview.md)) — slice 5.3 put the first EL0-composed text on
36	the serial line, and slice 5.4 puts a process's fd 1 and 2 on top of it.
37	
38	## Request-number ranges
39	
40	Every server's request numbers occupy a distinct band below `NOTIFY_MESSAGE`, so
41	a message type unambiguously identifies both its server and its meaning
42	(`kernel-shared/src/callnr.rs`, const-asserted disjoint). The bands are listed —
43	and rendered into the generated C header — in ascending numeric order. VFS took
44	`0x800` in slice 5.4; `0x900` and `0xA00` stay reserved for the two bands Phase 5
45	still owes, BDEV and MFS.
46	
47	| Base | Value | Server / purpose |
48	|------|-------|------------------|
49	| `PM_RQ_BASE`    | `0x700` | PM: `PM_GETPID` / `FORK` / `EXIT` / `WAIT` / `EXEC` |
50	| `VFS_RQ_BASE`   | `0x800` | VFS: `VFS_WRITE` |
51	| `CDEV_RQ_BASE`  | `0xB00` | Character drivers: `CDEV_WRITE` (TTY) |
52	| `VM_RQ_BASE`    | `0xC00` | VM: `VM_PAGEFAULT` / `BRK` / `MMAP` / `MUNMAP` / `FORK` |
53	| `SEF_RQ_BASE`   | `0xD00` | SEF control messages (ping / signal / init) |
54	| `DS_RQ_BASE`    | `0xE00` | DS: `DS_PUBLISH` / `RETRIEVE` / `CHECK` |
55	| `SCHED_RQ_BASE` | `0xF00` | SCHED: `SCHEDULING_NO_QUANTUM` / `START` / `STOP` / `SET_NICE` |
56

59	`server-rt` is minix.rs's small equivalent of MINIX 3's SEF (System Event
60	Framework). A server calls `sef_startup(SefConfig { init_fresh, signal_handler })`,
61	which learns the server's own endpoint and name from the kernel via
62	`SYS_GETINFO(GET_WHOAMI)`, runs the optional `init_fresh` callback, and returns a
63	`Sef` handle. The main loop is then `loop { if sef.receive(&mut msg) != 0 { continue } match msg.m_type { … } }`:
64	`sef.receive` wraps `ipc_receive(ANY, …)` and transparently handles SEF control
65	traffic — an RS heartbeat ping, a `SEF_SIGNAL` from PM/RS, a `SEF_INIT` — so the
66	server only sees genuine application messages.
67	
68	The classifier (`server-rt/src/classify.rs`, host-tested) gates each control
69	event on the message's *source*, not its type alone: an RS ping is only honored
70	from RS, a signal only from a signal manager, an init only from RS. A client
71	holding a mere `ipc_to` bit to the server cannot spoof one. `server-rt` is
72	`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` — callbacks travel in the config struct, not global
73	state. The `init_fresh` body most servers use is the shared
74	`sef_publish_to_ds(endpoint, name)` helper, which registers the server in DS.

## Where servers live

Servers are freestanding `#![no_std]` / `#![no_main]` ELF binaries linked with
their own `user.ld` (page-aligned segments based at `0x0010_0000`) and branded
with the minixrs ELF identity note, which the kernel requires of every image it
loads. The kernel's `build.rs` compiles each for the `aarch64-unknown-minixrs`
target and concatenates them into a single **MXBI archive** embedded in the
kernel image; the boot loader
(`kernel/src/arch/aarch64/userland.rs`) walks the archive and loads each module
into the proc slot named by its record. Each server gets its own per-process
TTBR0, so they all share the same low load base with no collision.

A server has no `println`. Its behaviour is observed through kernel-side traces
(`[ipc]`, `[ksys]`, `[pf]`, `[alarm]`), and since slice 5.1 it can also emit a
line itself through the kernel debug channel — `server-rt`'s `diag_print` /
`diag_fmt` issue a `SYS_DIAGCTL` carrying the text inline, which the kernel prints
prefixed with the caller's own name (`[diag vfs] …`). That is deliberately a
*debug* channel, not stdio: it exists to keep working while stdio itself is under
construction. Real console output arrives via the TTY driver (see
[Drivers](../drivers/overview.md)) — slice 5.3 put the first EL0-composed text on
the serial line, and slice 5.4 puts a process's fd 1 and 2 on top of it.

## Request-number ranges

Every server's request numbers occupy a distinct band below `NOTIFY_MESSAGE`, so
a message type unambiguously identifies both its server and its meaning
(`kernel-shared/src/callnr.rs`, const-asserted disjoint). The bands are listed —
and rendered into the generated C header — in ascending numeric order. VFS took
`0x800` in slice 5.4; `0x900` and `0xA00` stay reserved for the two bands Phase 5
still owes, BDEV and MFS.

| Base | Value | Server / purpose |
|------|-------|------------------|
| `PM_RQ_BASE`    | `0x700` | PM: `PM_GETPID` / `FORK` / `EXIT` / `WAIT` / `EXEC` |
| `VFS_RQ_BASE`   | `0x800` | VFS: `VFS_WRITE` |
| `CDEV_RQ_BASE`  | `0xB00` | Character drivers: `CDEV_WRITE` (TTY) |
| `VM_RQ_BASE`    | `0xC00` | VM: `VM_PAGEFAULT` / `BRK` / `MMAP` / `MUNMAP` / `FORK` |
| `SEF_RQ_BASE`   | `0xD00` | SEF control messages (ping / signal / init) |
| `DS_RQ_BASE`    | `0xE00` | DS: `DS_PUBLISH` / `RETRIEVE` / `CHECK` |
| `SCHED_RQ_BASE` | `0xF00` | SCHED: `SCHEDULING_NO_QUANTUM` / `START` / `STOP` / `SET_NICE` |

## SEF: the server runtime

`server-rt` is minix.rs's small equivalent of MINIX 3's SEF (System Event
Framework). A server calls `sef_startup(SefConfig { init_fresh, signal_handler })`,
which learns the server's own endpoint and name from the kernel via
`SYS_GETINFO(GET_WHOAMI)`, runs the optional `init_fresh` callback, and returns a
`Sef` handle. The main loop is then `loop { if sef.receive(&mut msg) != 0 { continue } match msg.m_type { … } }`:
`sef.receive` wraps `ipc_receive(ANY, …)` and transparently handles SEF control
traffic — an RS heartbeat ping, a `SEF_SIGNAL` from PM/RS, a `SEF_INIT` — so the
server only sees genuine application messages.

The classifier (`server-rt/src/classify.rs`, host-tested) gates each control
event on the message's *source*, not its type alone: an RS ping is only honored
from RS, a signal only from a signal manager, an init only from RS. A client
holding a mere `ipc_to` bit to the server cannot spoof one. `server-rt` is
`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` — callbacks travel in the config struct, not global
state. The `init_fresh` body most servers use is the shared
`sef_publish_to_ds(endpoint, name)` helper, which registers the server in DS.

165	## VFS: the write path
166	
167	**VFS** (`servers/vfs/`) turns a small integer into something you can write to.
168	That is the whole of its job in Phase 5 so far, and since slice 5.4 it does it for
169	real: an ordinary user process can `write(1, buf, len)` and see bytes on the
170	console. Mount points, `open`, and reads arrive with the MFS server in slice 5.8.
171	
172	### One request, one copy
173	
174	```text
175	user ──VFS_WRITE{fd,buf,len}──► VFS ──CDEV_WRITE{minor,gid,len,off}──► TTY
176	                                 │                                      │
177	                                 └── magic grant: caller's buf ──────────┘
178	                                         (kernel copies, once)
179	```
180	
181	VFS resolves the descriptor, issues a **magic** (third-party) grant naming the
182	*caller's* buffer with the driver as grantee, and forwards the grant id. TTY then
183	safecopies straight out of the caller's address space. The bytes never pass
184	through VFS: there is exactly one copy, from the process that wrote them to the
185	driver that transmits them. This is the first consumer of the magic grant form on
186	a real data path, and the rail slice 5.6's musl `write()` lands on.
187	
188	Three properties hold that path together:
189	
190	- **The grant's owner is the kernel-stamped `m_source`.** VFS holds `SYS_PROC`,
191	  which is what makes a magic grant legal for it at all — so a caller-supplied
192	  owner field would let any VFS client aim a privileged cross-address-space copy
193	  at a third party's memory. `VFS_WRITE` has no such field, and must never gain
194	  one. It is the same anti-confused-deputy rule that keeps a granter out of the
195	  `CDEV_WRITE` payload, applied to the granting side.
196	- **VFS absorbs short writes.** A character driver may move fewer bytes than asked
197	  (`CDEV_MAX_IO`, its staging limit); POSIX `write()` is not allowed to expose
198	  that, so VFS re-sends with `offset` advanced until the buffer is out and reports
199	  the total. One grant covers the whole buffer — only the offset moves. An error
200	  after partial progress reports the *progress*, since those bytes really did go
201	  out.
202	- **Every request gets a reply**, including an unknown one (`ENOSYS`). VFS's
203	  clients are all inside a SENDREC, so a dropped message blocks the caller forever.
204	
205	### The descriptor table
206	
207	`servers/vfs/src/fd.rs` holds one row of descriptors per process, indexed by
208	kernel proc number and sized from the shared `NR_SERVED_PROCS` ceiling that PM's
209	`mproc` and VM's `ClientRegions` also derive from. Nothing opens or closes yet, so
210	every row is identical — fds 0, 1, and 2 name the console, everything else is
211	`EBADF` — which is POSIX's inheritance convention and is what lets init write
212	before any filesystem exists. Because nothing mutates, the storage is an ordinary
213	immutable `static` and VFS carries no `unsafe`; slice 5.8's `open` flips it to the
214	`UnsafeCell` newtype that VM's region table already uses.
215	
216	VFS also remains the system's first *grant* client and first *console* client:
217	its startup still direct-grants a read-only buffer to PM (slice 5.2) and drives
218	`CDEV_WRITE` by hand (slice 5.3). Those are kept deliberately, as the regression
219	battery for three contracts the real write path never reaches — the direct-grant
220	form, a *visible* short write, and the two `CDEV_WRITE` refusals a well-formed
221	`write()` cannot provoke.
222	
223	## init: PID 1
224	
225	**init** (`userland/init/`) is the first real user process and the live exercise
226	for everything above. Unlike the demo stubs it replaced, it is a genuine boot
227	module: `build.rs` packs it into the MXBI archive with its true proc number

`servers/vfs/src/fd.rs` holds one row of descriptors per process, indexed by
kernel proc number and sized from the shared `NR_SERVED_PROCS` ceiling that PM's
`mproc` and VM's `ClientRegions` also derive from. Every row *starts* identical —
fds 0, 1, and 2 name the console, everything else is `EBADF` — which is POSIX's
inheritance convention and is what lets init write before any filesystem exists.
Slice 5.8's `open` is what makes rows diverge, and it moved the storage to the
`UnsafeCell` newtype VM's region table already uses. That brings a rule with it:
**never hold a borrow of the table across a SENDREC**. `Fd` is `Copy` precisely so
that is easy to obey — a resolve's borrow dies at the destructuring `let`, and the
handler carries values into the round trip.

`open` hands out the **lowest free descriptor**, POSIX's rule and the only thing
about it a client can observe without reading the file: close one and the next
`open` reuses that number. `close` frees the slot and sends the filesystem
nothing, because MFS keeps no per-open state — which is also why the FS band has
no `PUTNODE`.

### The read path, and its two copies

```text
user ──VFS_OPEN{path,len}───► VFS ──SYS_COPY──────────► (the path, into VFS)
                               │
                               └──FS_LOOKUP{path}─────► MFS  → (ino, mode)

user ──VFS_READ{fd,buf,len}──► VFS ──FS_READ{ino,gid,len,pos}──► MFS
                                │                                 │
                                └── magic grant: caller's buf ────┘
```

Two copies, not one, and the difference from the write path is deliberate: MFS
stages a block through its own buffer before safecopying the requested slice out
of it. A MinixFS read is rarely block-aligned in both the file and the
destination, and a *hole* has no device block to copy from at all — so the staging
cannot be elided. This is MINIX 3's own shape. Only the second copy is VFS's
grant; the bytes still never pass through VFS.

Two more properties, each with its own boot marker:

- **`SYS_COPY` reads the path, and its source is the kernel-stamped `m_source`.**
  This is the first live consumer of decision D4's "`SYS_COPY` for small
  control-plane reads" sentence, and the confused-deputy rule in its sharpest
  form: `SYS_COPY` has *no per-target authorization whatsoever* — the caller's
  `k_call_mask` bit is the whole check — so a payload-supplied source process
  would let any client read any process's memory through VFS.
- **VFS does not loop on read.** It loops on `write` because a driver's staging
  limit may not reach `write()`'s return value; `read()` is explicitly allowed to
  return less than asked for, and a file read is short at EOF regardless. EOF is a
  read returning `0` — no file's size is cached anywhere along the path, so that
  is the single source of truth.

VFS also remains the system's first *grant* client and first *console* client:
its startup still direct-grants a read-only buffer to PM (slice 5.2) and drives
`CDEV_WRITE` by hand (slice 5.3). Those are kept deliberately, as the regression
battery for three contracts the real write path never reaches — the direct-grant
form, a *visible* short write, and the two `CDEV_WRITE` refusals a well-formed
`write()` cannot provoke. Slice 5.7's block-device demo, by contrast, is **gone**:
MFS is the real BDEV client now, so the battery moved there and VFS is back to
knowing nothing about block devices.

## MFS: the file system

**MFS** (`fs/mfs/`) is the first file system in minix.rs, read-only as of slice
5.8. It sits between VFS and a block driver, and it is the piece that makes a path
resolve to bytes: VFS asks `FS_LOOKUP` for an inode and `FS_READ` for its
contents, and MFS answers by fetching blocks from the `memory` ramdisk over BDEV
and decoding them with the `minixrs-mfs` format library (`superblock`, `inode`,
`layout`, `dirent`, `read`) that slice 5.7 already shipped and host-tested.

The crate is split unusually hard. Its `[[bin]]` carries
`required-features = ["server"]` so the format library stays a one-dependency
crate the kernel's build script can use for free — and the price is that **the
binary is invisible to every CI job except the QEMU boot smoke test**. So every
line with a decision in it lives in the library (`proto.rs` for the wire codec,
`walk.rs` for traversal and read policy), and `main.rs` is SEF/IPC/grant glue.

Three things characterise the server itself:

- **One 4 KiB block buffer, in `.bss`.** A boot server's stack is exactly one page
  and a block is exactly one page, so the buffer cannot be a local — the frame
  base would land below the mapping, and VM turns that fault into a SIGSEGV that
  prints nothing the forbidden-marker list catches. It is reached only through a
  `Blocks` capability token whose `read(&mut self) -> &[u8; N]` makes "hold a
  directory block across the next fetch" a *borrow-check error* rather than a
  promise. Every intermediate the walk needs is a small `Copy` value.
- **Streaming, not buffering.** `tools/mkfs-mfs`'s `verify.rs` is the reference
  implementation of the same reader, but it materializes a whole directory into a
  `Vec`; MFS asks about one block at a time and keeps nothing but a `u32`. The
  `fs.selfcheck` boot marker is the one place the two readers meet over a real
  image.
- **Degraded, never fatal.** Past `sef_startup` nothing panics and nothing spins:
  a failed mount answers `ENODEV` to every request, and every device-derived loop
  bound has a cap, because a corrupt inode claiming `size = i32::MAX` would
  otherwise spin MFS — which would block VFS, which would block init.

Two error-relay rules sit side by side and read as contradictory. A failed
`BDEV_READ` becomes `EIO`, because MFS's client addressed a *file* and the device
beneath it is an implementation detail. A failed `SYS_SAFECOPY` against VFS's
grant is relayed **verbatim**, because `EPERM` ("your grant does not authorize
this") and `EFAULT` ("your buffer is not mapped") are different bugs on the
caller's side.

**Goal:** files readable through the full VFS→MFS→BDEV→ramdisk stack.

**Scope:** `fs/mfs` server half (roster +1, proc_nr 6): SEF loop serving

per D13), PUTNODE, READ (data moved by magic grant direct to the
requester's buffer), STAT-lite. VFS: lazy root mount on first open;

fd table; read path forwards a magic grant to MFS. Sonar `fs/**/src/main.rs`
exclusion + miri list addition land here with the code. May split a/b
(MFS half / VFS half) like 4.6 — one slice number.

**Proof:** init opens `/etc/motd`, reads it, writes it to fd 1 — the motd
text crosses BDEV→MFS→VFS→TTY and lands on serial.

### Slice 5.8: MFS server (read-only) + FS band + VFS mount/open/read ◀ ready (branch `feature/slice-5.8-mfs-server`, pending merge)

**Goal:** files readable through the full VFS→MFS→BDEV→ramdisk stack.

**Shipped as two commits on one branch** (5.8a MFS half, 5.8b VFS half), boot
green at each — the a/b split this entry anticipated.

**Scope, as built.** `fs/mfs` server half (roster +1, proc_nr 6, packed between
`memory` and `vfs`): SEF loop serving `FS_RQ_BASE = 0x900`. The request set is
**`FS_READSUPER` + `FS_LOOKUP` + `FS_READ` only** — three departures from this
entry's original list, each deliberate:

- **No `PUTNODE`.** MFS keeps no per-open state, so there is no node to put.
- **No STAT-lite / `VFS_STAT`.** `FS_LOOKUP`'s reply already carries mode and
  size, which is the whole of what a client needs before reading.
- **No GETDENTS.** Nothing consumes it — the `CDEV_READ` precedent that a request
  without a consumer is better absent than stubbed.

The path travels **inline** (NUL-padded, `FS_PATH_MAX = 64`), not by grant: it is
control plane, it costs MFS no staging buffer, and it deletes the confused-deputy
question outright. Data travels by grant, with no granter and no grant-offset
field. An over-long `FS_READ` is **clamped** (a short read), the deliberate
departure back towards `CDEV_WRITE` and away from `BDEV_READ`.

`0x900` was the last reserved band slot, so `0x700..0xC00` is now fully
allocated; the callnr test that recorded it as free is replaced by one recording
that it is not.

VFS: `VFS_OPEN`/`VFS_READ`/`VFS_CLOSE` (`NR_VFS_MSGS` 1→4), lazy root mount whose
*failure is not cached*, `write.rs` renamed `rw.rs` (read reuses write's payload
and `advance`'s rules are direction-agnostic) plus a new `open.rs`, and an fd
table that is now interior-mutable with `Fd::File { ino, pos }` and `NR_FDS` 4→8.
VFS's slice-5.7 `bdev_demo`/`bdev_denials` **retire** — MFS is the real BDEV
client, so the battery relocates there and VFS goes back to knowing nothing about
block devices. Sonar `fs/**/src/main.rs` exclusion landed with the code; the miri
`-p` entry already existed.

Two hazards found during design, both real:

1. init's `("no-such", VFS_WRITE + 1, …)` probe would have become `VFS_OPEN` and
   silently retired the `vfs.deny ok n=4` marker. Fixed to the band-relative
   `VFS_RQ_BASE + NR_VFS_MSGS`.
2. `[[bin]] required-features = ["server"]` removes `fs/mfs/src/main.rs` from
   every CI job. Mitigated by a lib-heavy layout (`proto.rs`/`walk.rs` hold every
   decision), one extra clippy step in `ci.yml`, and a note in `Cargo.toml`.

**Proof.** MFS's own prologue is self-driving: `[as] mfs nr=6`,
`[diag mfs] sef ready`, `bdev.ds ok ep=`, `mount ok root=1 bs=4096 blocks=256`,
`fs.selfcheck ok n=31 match=1`, `fs.indirect ok match=1` (the only marker that
reaches the single-indirect arm), `bdev.tail ok match=1`, `bdev.deny ok n=10`.
Then VFS: `fs.ds ok ep=`, `fs.mount ok root=1 bs=4096 blocks=256`,
`fs.deny ok n=10`. Then the milestone — **`minix.rs rootfs: motd from MFS`**,
`/etc/motd` read by init and written to fd 1 — plus `fs.read ok match=1` (bytes
moved *and* `pos` advanced *and* EOF is `0`), `fs.fd ok match=1` (open→3, open→4,
close both, re-open→3), and `open.deny ok n=8`. Retired: `bdev.read ok n=32` and
`bdev.head ok match=1`, strictly subsumed by `mount ok`.
